analysis: The only change in this PR is documentation in docs/developer/test.md (head lines 2115-2131). It adds a test-instruction paragraph for the 'Model Requant Upload' workflow: `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/models -p 'test_*.py'`. It describes a secret-free preflight, a job in the `prod` environment limited to master, a check that prints only pass/fail, an upload that holds only the chosen key set and only after this run's check passed, tools pinned by hash, and a selftest before any secret. I examined both supplied head units (lines 1807-2730). No code, workflow, permission, key-handling, attestation or crypto behavior changes in this diff, and the added text introduces no secrets or commands that weaken a control. The relevant retained definition, T-041 (prefix cache), is not touched. The rest of the test.md text in the units is unchanged context, mostly test and qualification instructions. It consistently disclaims that CPU-only or fixture checks establish deployment, native quality or security. The doc describes the workflow and scripts/models tests, which are not in the supplied evidence. I therefore cannot verify that the described behavior (master-only gating, hash-pinned tools, selftest before secrets) matches the actual `.github/workflows` and `scripts/models` files. If those files are in the same PR, the next pass should check that those controls are implemented as documented. This is a coverage limit, not a finding. No threat-model update is needed from this doc-only change.
